title: A Step Beyond BRET: Fluorescence by Unbound Excitation from Luminescence (FUEL)
protocol: Purchase or develop luminescent bacteria and appropriate culture media such as modified Escherichia coli expressing the luxABCDE21, Vibrio fischeri, Photobacterium sp., and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Prepare physiological saline (0.9% NaCl) according to standard recipes.
Prepare culture media solutions for E. coli and K. pneumoniae in Luria Bertani (LB) at 37 °C.
Prepare culture media solutions for V. fischeri and Photobacterium sp. in LB supplemented with 0.5 M NaCl at 22 °C.
Purchase or acquire fluorescent probes such as Q-tracker 705, Q-tracker 800, fluorescent polystyrene microspheres, and conventional fluorescent dyes.
Ensure access to a whole animal bioluminescence imager capable of detecting signal under a wide range of emission wavelengths and exposure times.
Prepare the necessary reagents for bacterial labeling.
Start overnight cultures of luminescent bacteria from individual colonies on standard culture plates.
Initiate fresh subcultures the day of experimentation and allow them to progress until an OD600 of 1-1.5 is achieved.
Combine aliquots of 100 μl from each culture with either 5 μl of QD705 or physiological saline (PS).
Add to 895 μl of PS into standard spectroscopic cuvettes.
Place the filled cuvettes into the IVIS Spectrum and take the measurements under the appropriate filter sets.
Fill two reduced volume (1 ml) plastic photometric cuvettes with either 50 μl of QD705 or 97.2 μl of non-fluorescent 48 nm polystyrene microspheres in a total volume of 1 ml PS.
Prepare a light source cuvette by encasing a third cuvette with standard black tape.
Carefully prepare two identical optical windows on opposite sides of the cuvette.
Place previously filled cuvettes directly onto either side of the light source cuvette.
Add a 1 ml aliquot of V. fischeri or other culture (e.g., luminescent E. coli) from a fresh subculture into the light source cuvette.
Cover with an opaque material, such as black paper to reduce any light contamination.
Visualize three cuvettes under Total Light emission filter with an exposure time of 10 seconds.
Visualize the same cuvettes under 710-730 nm emission filters with a 30-second exposure time.
Reposition external cuvettes at equivalent distances and visualize again.
Repeat repositioning until a face-to-face distance of 3 cm is achieved between cuvettes.
Acquire fluorescence images (450-480 nm excitation, 710-730 nm emission) to validate QD705 location at each step.
Fill two reduced volume cuvettes with 1 ml solutions containing a fluorophore or fluorescent nanoparticle in one and PS or PS with non-fluorescent nanoparticles as negative control in the other.
Add a 1 ml aliquot of fresh V. fischeri to a blacked-out third cuvette containing two optical windows on opposite sides.
Place the two reduced volume cuvettes at an equal distance from the blacked-out cuvette, then visualize under appropriate filters with a distance of 0.7 cm between cuvettes.
Repeat visualization with other fluorophores and nanoparticles as outlined in Table 1.
Biotinylate primary antibodies specific to K. pneumoniae using EZ-Link Sulfo-NHS-LC-Biotin.
Remove excess reagent from the biotinylated antibodies using desalting columns under centrifugation (1,500 x g) for 2 min.
Determine protein concentration of biotinylated antibodies using a Bradford assay.
Measure degree of antibody biotinylation by HABA assay.
Mix 100 μl of biotinylated solution with 40 μl α-Kp antibody to obtain α-Kp-biot batches.
Wash K. pneumoniae in 1x PBS and resuspend in 1x PBS to an OD of 4 (ca. 4 x 108 CFU ml-1).
Incubate 100 μl PBS, α-Kp antibodies or PBS for control, with 100 μl cells for 90 min at 30 °C.
Wash the cells three times in 1x PBS and resuspend in 196 μl PBS.
Label the cells with QD705 streptavidin conjugate and divide them into two equivalent volumes.
Wash one solution three times and then resuspend it into appropriate volume.
Distribute 100 μl of the washed solution into individual wells of a black 96-well plate.
Distribute 100 μl of the unwashed solution into individual wells of a black 96-well plate.
Measure luminescence under the Total Light filter.
Measure luminescence under the 490-510 nm filter.
Measure luminescence under the 710-730 nm filter.
Determine fluorophore concentration using 450-480 nm excitation and 710-730 nm emission.
